# active profiles config
#
# the application uses two active profiles
#
# one - for select database
# ------------------------------------------------
# When using HSQL, use: hsqldb

# ------------------------------------------------

server.servlet.context-path=/petclinic/

# active profiles config
#
# application use two active profiles
#
# one for select repository layer
# ------------------------------------------------
# When using HSQL, use: hsqldb
# When using MySQL, use: mysql
# When using PostgeSQL, use: postgres
# ------------------------------------------------
#
# one - for select database
# ------------------------------------------------
# When using Spring jpa, use: jpa
# When using Spring JDBC, use: jdbc
# When using Spring Data JPA, use: spring-data-jpa
# ------------------------------------------------

spring.profiles.active=hsqldb,spring-data-jpa

# ------------------------------------------------

server.port=9966
server.servlet.context-path=/petclinic/
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# database init
spring.sql.init.schema-locations=classpath*:db/${spring.sql.init.platform}/schema.sql
spring.sql.init.data-locations=classpath*:db/${spring.sql.init.platform}/data.sql

logging.level.org.springframework=INFO
#logging.level.org.springframework=DEBUG

# enable the desired authentication type
# by default the authentication is disabled

# REST version of Spring PetClinic Sample Application (spring-framework-petclinic extension)

[![Java Build Status](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/maven-build-master.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/maven-build-master.yml)
[![Docker Build Status](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/docker-build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/actions/workflows/docker-build.yml)
[![Quality Gate Status](https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_badges/measure?project=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest&metric=alert_status)](https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest)
[![Coverage](https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_badges/measure?project=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest&metric=coverage)](https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=spring-petclinic_spring-petclinic-rest)

This backend version of the Spring Petclinic application only provides a REST API. **There is no UI**.
The [spring-petclinic-angular project](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-angular) is a Angular front-end application which consumes the REST API.

## Understanding the Spring Petclinic application with a few diagrams

[See the presentation of the Spring Petclinic Framework version](http://fr.slideshare.net/AntoineRey/spring-framework-petclinic-sample-application)

### Petclinic ER Model

![alt petclinic-ermodel](petclinic-ermodel.png)

## Running Petclinic locally

### With Maven command line
```sh
git clone https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest.git
cd spring-petclinic-rest
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

### With Docker
```sh
docker run -p 9966:9966 springcommunity/spring-petclinic-rest
```

You can then access petclinic here: [http://localhost:9966/petclinic/](http://localhost:9966/petclinic/)

There is an actuator health check route as well:
* [http://localhost:9966/petclinic/actuator/health](http://localhost:9966/petclinic/actuator/health)

## 📖 OpenAPI REST API Documentation
This project provides a RESTful API for managing a veterinary clinic's **owners, pets, veterinarians, visits, and specialties**.

content.text:
Green. Here's a summary of the change.

## What I implemented

The spec: a new owner's `membershipLevel` is capped at one above the highest `membershipLevel` among their existing household members (owners sharing the same last name + postcode); with no existing household member, no cap.

**1. New util `LevelCeiling.java`** — a small, self-contained class (no surrounding complexity) that reuses the existing `Household` and `Membership` helpers:

```java
public static int cap(int level, Owner owner, Collection<Owner> allOwners) {
    // max membership level among other, non-deleted household members; +1; else no cap
}
```

**2. `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — one line applies the cap to the returned DTO right after mapping (so it also feeds the audit log):

```java
ownerDto.setMembershipLevel(LevelCeiling.cap(ownerDto.getMembershipLevel(), owner, this.clinicService.findAllOwners()));
```

## One necessary interaction I had to resolve

The new test creates two owners in the *same* household — which the feature is fundamentally about ("household **members**", plural). But the pre-existing `DuplicateHouseholdException.rejectIfDuplicate` call rejected the second one with **409** before the cap could ever apply, so the test couldn't create the household it needed. True duplicate registrations are already caught upstream by `IdentityKey.rejectIfDuplicate` (telephone+email); the household check was specifically rejecting *distinct people in the same household* — i.e. exactly the household members this rule governs.
